papers.title_en: CytoWave: Perturbation-Centric Pretraining for Single-Cell Response Prediction
papers.authors: Yuwei Miao, Jingquan Yan, Hehuan Ma, Thao M. Dang, Lin Xu, Siyuan Zhang, Junzhou Huang
papers.evidence: 面向单细胞遗传扰动响应预测的扰动中心预训练框架
papers.tldr: 单细胞扰动响应预测是建模细胞反应的关键任务，但现有方法因实验协议、生物背景和物种差异难以跨数据集泛化。CytoWave以扰动为中心进行预训练，先用同源映射统一大规模跨物种扰动数据，再分两阶段训练：第一阶段在未扰动细胞上通过掩码基因表达恢复学习参照对照状态，第二阶段给定对照状态和扰动信号预测扰动后基因表达，并用对比目标对齐扰动响应的隐表示与扰动信号。在严格留出数据集的多条件组合评估及通路活性变化案例中，CytoWave均表现稳定有效，为跨数据集、跨物种的扰动响应预测提供了可泛化框架。
papers.abstract_en: Predicting gene expression under perturbations from single-cell data is a fundamental task for modeling cellular responses, with applications in discovering gene function and designing therapeutics. However, existing methods often struggle to generalize across datasets due to differences in experimental protocols, biological contexts, and species. We present \textbf{CytoWave}, a perturbation-centric pretraining framework for single-cell genetic perturbation response prediction. We leverage large-scale cross-species perturbation datasets unified via orthology and train CytoWave in a two-stage manner. In the first stage, we learn reference control cell states via masked gene expression recovery on unperturbed cells. In the second stage, we pretrain the model to predict perturbed gene expression given control states and perturbation signals, together with a contrastive objective that aligns latent representations of perturbation responses with perturbation signals. We perform strict dataset-held-out evaluation across multiple condition combinations and case studies of pathway activity changes, demonstrating consistent and effective performance of CytoWave in predicting single-cell genetic perturbation responses.

papers.title_en: scBIG++: Learning Across Genes and Cells to Predict Single-Cell Perturbation Responses
papers.authors: Jiafa Ruan, Zican Qiao, Zongxin Yang, Ruijie Quan, Yi Yang
papers.evidence: 全基因单细胞扰动响应预测框架
papers.tldr: 现有扰动预测多聚焦高变基因，限制表达变化分析，也忽略同干预下细胞的异质响应。scBIG++用基因关系聚类构建共享窗口，以Dynamic SoftSub学习表达依赖子模块，并结合Set-GCAE与潜变量流生成全基因表达。六类遗传和化学数据中，它在未见靶点、组合、跨细胞系及留出化合物上恢复扰动效应并重建全基因表达，为下游调控分析提供更完整视图。
papers.abstract_en: Predicting single-cell transcriptional responses to genetic and chemical interventions supports gene-function discovery and regulatory analysis. Existing studies often focus only on highly variable genes, restricting the expression changes available for downstream analysis. Cells exposed to the same intervention can also show heterogeneous expression responses, with coordinated gene programs active to different degrees. We propose scBIG++, a full-gene perturbation prediction framework that models this heterogeneity by connecting expression-adaptive gene modules with population-conditioned generation. To preserve shared gene structure while accommodating cellular variation, Gene-Relation Clustering organizes genes into common windows, within which Dynamic SoftSub learns expression-dependent submodule memberships. This shared organization enables Set-GCAE to exchange information about corresponding gene groups across control cells, placing individual representations in their source-population context. The cell representations initialize a latent flow, while their pooled summary and the perturbation representation condition response generation. Generated states are decoded into expression profiles covering all assayed protein-coding genes retained after preprocessing, supporting comprehensive analysis of perturbation-induced expression changes. Experiments across six genetic and chemical settings spanning 6,539--19,451 genes demonstrate competitive perturbation-effect recovery and full-gene expression reconstruction under unseen targets and combinations, cross-cell-line transfer, and held-out compounds. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/ttruan2426-dot/scBIG.

papers.title_en: Predicting Single-Cell Spatial Gene Expression from H&E using Pathology Foundation Models
papers.authors: Ashley P. Tsang, Evan Liu, Conrad Foo, Bob Chen, Hassaan Maan, Donny Chan, Elisa Penna, Veronica Ibarra Lopez, Hector Corrada Bravo, Aicha BenTaieb, Lisa M. McGinnis, Runmin Wei, Kenneth T. Gao
papers.evidence: 改造病理基础模型从H&E预测单细胞空间基因表达
papers.tldr: 从H&E图像预测单细胞空间基因表达，有望低成本获取空间分子信息，但病理基础模型的图块级预训练可能难以捕捉细粒度细胞特征。作者系统评估并设计领域知识与任务特定的适配策略，在配对H&E与Xenium 5K数据上适配模型。结果显示，基因级Pearson相关较零样本基线提升2.67倍，全基因面板AUROC达0.800，空间可变基因相关最高为0.643。该工作表明H&E表征可恢复有生物学意义的空间表达模式，同时揭示细胞分辨率形态推断的潜力与局限。
papers.abstract_en: Predicting gene expression directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images offers a scalable and cost-effective approach to deriving spatial molecular insights from routine histology. Pathology foundation models, typically pretrained using tile-level objectives, may not adequately capture the fine-grained cellular features required for single-cell molecular prediction. In this work, we systematically evaluate and establish domain-informed and task-specific strategies for adapting pathology foundation models to single-cell spatial gene expression prediction. Using paired H&E and Xenium 5K data, our approach improves mean gene-wise Pearson correlation by 2.67x over the standard zero-shot baseline and achieves state-of-the-art performance on this task. We demonstrate strong gene-detection performance across the full gene panel (AUROC = 0.800) and importantly identify that predictive performance varies substantially across biological contexts, with our model achieving its highest Pearson correlation for spatially variable genes (r = 0.643). Our findings demonstrate that, despite the challenges of sparse single-cell measurements, H&E-derived representations can recover biologically meaningful spatial expression patterns, highlighting both the opportunities and limitations of morphology-based molecular inference at cellular resolution.

papers.title_en: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS
papers.authors: Conci, R., D'Ascenzo, D., Cultrera di Montesano, S., Raghavan, S., Winter, P. S., Van Allen, E. M., Crawford, L., Lotter, W.
papers.evidence: 预测单细胞扰动响应分布的生成式框架，并采用实验校准评测
papers.tldr: 单细胞扰动图谱难以穷举所有生物背景、扰动与剂量组合，亟需预测未测条件下的细胞响应分布。GENESIS以实验条件协变量为输入，用轻量神经网络和能量评分训练生成模型。在Tahoe-100M与PBMC细胞因子图谱中，它显著优于现有生成模型和统计基线，并在独立重复条件上接近实验可重复性。该工作还提出以实验可重复性校准误差的评估框架，并显示更广但较浅的测量有助于扩大覆盖和补全稀疏样本。
papers.abstract_en: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

papers.title_en: From WSIs to Bulk, Spatial and Single-Cell Transcriptomics via Multi-Scale Graph Neural Networks
papers.authors: Miguel Andrade, José Almeida, Carlos Santiago, Catarina Barata
papers.evidence: 用多尺度图神经网络从全切片病理图像预测空间转录组
papers.tldr: 空间与单细胞转录组信息精细但昂贵稀缺，WSI联合bulk RNA则更易获取。本文提出多尺度图神经网络，用UNI2-h提取形态特征，在patch和细胞层级构图，从WSI同时预测bulk、空间与单细胞表达。模型在TCGA、Visium、Xenium的肺肾乳腺数据上联合训练，并以跨尺度一致性损失约束。结果slide级预测较准、patch级中等（Xenium最强）、单细胞级中等，且支持生存分析、空间风险图和分子分型。
papers.abstract_en: Understanding the spatial distribution of gene expression is key to studying complex diseases like cancer. While Spatial Transcriptomics (ST) and Single-Cell Transcriptomics (scT) provide high-resolution insights, they remain expensive and scarce. In contrast, standard histopathology Whole-Slide Images (WSIs) paired with bulk RNA sequencing are widely available. This work introduces a Multi-Scale Graph Neural Network (GNN) capable of simultaneously predicting bulk, spatial, and single-cell transcriptomics directly from WSIs. By extracting morphological features using a Pathology Foundation Model (PFM) (UNI2-h) and constructing spatial graphs at both patch and cell levels, the model learns the hierarchical relationships within the tissue. The network is trained on a combined dataset of The Cancer Genome Atlas Program (TCGA), Visium, and Xenium samples across lung, kidney, and breast tissues. A hybrid training strategy is employed, leveraging direct supervision alongside weakly supervised consistency losses to ensure predictions align across biological scales. Results show the model accurately predicts gene expression at the slide level and moderately at the patch level (strongest on Xenium), and achieves moderate correlation at the challenging single-cell level. Furthermore, downstream tasks explore the clinical relevance of these predictions, demonstrating their utility in survival analysis, spatial hazard mapping, and tumor classification via molecular signatures.

papers.title_en: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction
papers.authors: Zheyu Zhang, Yuanhao Huang, Fan Feng, Jie Liu
papers.evidence: 审计基础模型扰动响应预测的可靠性
papers.tldr: 基础模型扰动预测多按总体精度评估，难以判断单条预测是否可靠。作者审计STATE的ST解码器，发现首层注意力输出低秩，投影到4–32个固定方向仍保留PDC。PDC随预测响应到最近训练响应的余弦距离增大而下降，据此提出predicted-NN-distance置信度。该分数与PDC的Spearman相关达0.81，阈值可跨编码器和细胞系迁移，并可预测药物扰动。
papers.abstract_en: Foundation-model predictors of perturbation response are evaluated primarily by aggregate accuracy. Using their predictions to prioritize experiments requires assessing each prediction's reliability. We audit the state-transition (ST) decoder used in STATE across three encoders (SE-600M, scGPT, and Tahoe-x1) and four cell lines under CRISPRi. The decoder's first attention layer has a low-rank output. Projecting this output onto 4-32 fixed directions estimated from training activations preserves mean per-perturbation Pearson delta correlation (PDC). This low-rank attention bottleneck bounds the decoder's reliability by distance to training responses: PDC declines as the cosine distance from a perturbation's observed response to its nearest training response increases. We propose predicted-NN-distance, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, as a per-prediction confidence score. The score has a mean absolute Spearman correlation of 0.81 with PDC, close to the 0.88 obtained with the observed response. Thresholds calibrated on this score transfer across encoders and cell lines, and the score remains predictive of PDC for drug perturbations.

papers.title_en: The Delta Gap: Cellular World Models for Perturbation Response Prediction Are Far Harder Than Global Correlation Implies
papers.authors: Junhui Gao
papers.evidence: 细胞世界模型用于扰动响应预测的评测分析
papers.tldr: 细胞扰动响应模型通常用全局Pearson相关评估，但该指标被大量非响应基因主导，严重虚高。作者在Replogle K562上提出delta空间评估，揭示GEARS全局相关0.977而delta相关仅0.076的“delta gap”。进一步用RWR、kNN后处理及delta对齐训练定位并缩小差距，delta相关提升至0.179/0.217，并可零样本迁移至Norman A549。该工作首次系统量化评估伪影，强调扰动表示几何是关键瓶颈。
papers.abstract_en: Cellular world models aim to predict how cells respond to genetic perturbations, analogous to world models in reinforcement learning. Perturbation response models are evaluated almost exclusively by global Pearson correlation between predicted and observed transcriptomes. We show this metric is dominated by thousands of non-responsive genes and severely inflates apparent performance. On the Replogle K562 screen (509 unseen perturbations, 5000 genes), GEARS achieves global Pearson 0.977, but its delta Pearson is only 0.076. A trivial baseline predicting mean training delta achieves 0.267, which is 3.5x better than GEARS. Our primary contribution is methodological: we identify and quantify this delta gap as a systematic evaluation artifact, and propose delta-space evaluation as the primary benchmark. We provide two post-hoc corrections (RWR on co-expression graphs and kNN matching) and show that 2.8x of the remaining gap lies in perturbation representation geometry, not decoder capacity. We further show the gap is partially addressable end-to-end: delta-aligned training (lambda = 3.0) raises delta Pearson to 0.179 on Replogle (2.35x over GEARS) and surpasses the trivial baseline on direction accuracy (0.680 vs 0.567) and gene recovery (1.52 vs 1.19); combined with kNN it reaches 0.217. An amplitude-calibration variant (eta = 0.3) further raises gene recovery to 2.16 while reaching 0.218. Critically, these representations transfer zero-shot across cell lines: from Replogle K562 to unseen Norman A549, the delta-aligned model reaches 0.328 on 741 shared genes, 4.7x a trivial baseline and 2.1x standard GEARS. This is the first systematic quantification of the delta gap, and the first diagnostic framework localizing the residual gap to perturbation representation geometry via an oracle upper bound.

papers.title_en: Continuous 3D Spatial Transcriptomics Reconstruction via Histology-Informed Implicit Neural Representations
papers.authors: Kaito Shiku, Ryoma Bise, Ahtisham Fazeel Abbasi, Yuichiro Iwashita, Shumpei Takezaki, Andreas Dengel, Muhammad Nabeel Asim
papers.evidence: 组织学信息驱动的隐式神经表示，利用组织学图像预测基因表达
papers.tldr: 三维空间转录组需从离散二维切片重建，但切片常因成本高而稀疏采样。本文提出组织学引导的多任务隐式神经表示HIM-INR，以共享骨干联合重建基因表达与组织学表征，并用密集组织学图像提供辅助空间监督。训练完成后，模型无需组织学图像即可在任意三维坐标预测基因表达。在两个3D ST数据集上，HIM-INR重建效果优于现有方法，缺失切片越多优势越明显，为稀疏3D ST的连续重建提供了有效方案。
papers.abstract_en: Three-dimensional spatial transcriptomics (3D ST) enables the analysis of gene-expression patterns across tissue depths. However, 3D ST measurements are acquired from discrete 2D tissue sections, which are often sparsely sampled due to high acquisition costs. To address this limitation, we propose a histology-informed multi-task implicit neural representation (HIM-INR) for continuous 3D gene-expression reconstruction from sparse ST observations. HIM-INR jointly reconstructs gene-expression profiles and histological representations using an INR with a shared backbone, leveraging densely sampled histological images as auxiliary spatial supervision. Once trained, HIM-INR predicts gene expression at arbitrary 3D coordinates without requiring histological images. Experiments on two 3D ST datasets demonstrate improved reconstruction over existing methods, particularly as the number of missing ST sections increases.

papers.title_en: Digital twins forecast individual immune trajectories
papers.authors: Hu, C., Yu, C., Chen, C. Y.-C.
papers.evidence: 将共享虚拟细胞模型个性化构建为个体数字孪生
papers.tldr: 人体免疫状态高度个体化，现有预测多依赖单次挑战前测量和人群汇总模式，难以刻画个人变化。ImmuneTwins用个体单细胞观测个性化共享虚拟细胞模型，随新数据更新数字孪生。它在两个外部队列将免疫年龄误差降低32%和42%，重复流感疫苗接种中变化方向预测准确率提高35%，误差随观测累积下降27%。该工作确立了可预测个体免疫轨迹并识别特征免疫标志的虚拟细胞数字孪生。
papers.abstract_en: The human immune system differs markedly between individuals and changes in response to infection, vaccination and treatment. AI virtual cells are being built to simulate cellular responses to perturbation. Yet these models, like most immune-response predictors, describe each person by a single pre-challenge measurement and forecast change from patterns pooled across people. Digital twins, updated with every new observation of an individual, could forecast how that person's immune state changes. Here we present ImmuneTwins, which builds these twins from single-cell profiles by personalizing a shared virtual-cell model with each individual's observations. In two external populations, ImmuneTwins reduced immune-age error by 32% and 42% relative to the best existing method. During repeated influenza vaccination, its twins predicted the direction of immune-cell change 35% more accurately than the best published method, and their error fell by 27% as observations accumulated. The twins revealed that immune cells and plasma proteins recover about half their deviation from a persistent personal reference within 90 days, whereas response size varies between challenges. They further localized B-cell remodelling in exceptional longevity and anticipated patient-specific immune trajectories during myeloma treatment. These results establish virtual-cell digital twins for forecasting individual immune change and identifying each person's characteristic immune features.

papers.title_en: EMBER: Contextualized gene representations enable compositional prediction across cellular perturbations
papers.authors: Ho, N., Xing, E. P., Ma, J.
papers.evidence: 对单一与组合扰动效应的组合式预测
papers.tldr: 预测单基因与组合扰动效应需要能整合功能关系与细胞状态、并可跨任务迁移的基因表示。EMBER以基因中心基础模型，结合交互引导对比学习与掩码表达重建，在多样且平衡采样的单细胞语料上预训练。它冻结编码器，用轻量探针组合上下文基因嵌入，统一支持单基因响应、双基因互作和多靶点药物响应预测。该方法提升跨情境预测与遗传互作排序，并优先识别mTOR抑制下的SCFD1候选依赖。
papers.abstract_en: Predicting the effects of individual and combined perturbations is central to identifying context-specific vulnerabilities and designing targeted interventions. Yet learning gene representations that integrate functional relationships with cellular state and transfer across perturbation tasks remains challenging. Here, we present EMBER, a gene-centric foundation model that learns context-dependent functional representations of genes. EMBER combines interaction-guided contrastive learning with masked expression reconstruction during pretraining on a single-cell corpus curated for diversity and balanced sampling across cell types and experimental batches. EMBER decouples gene representation learning from task-specific prediction through a composable embedding framework: the pretrained encoder remains frozen, while lightweight probes combine contextualized gene embeddings to predict individual and combined perturbation effects. The same pretrained representations support single-gene perturbation-response prediction, digenic interaction prediction, and multi-target drug-response prediction. EMBER improves cross-context perturbation-response prediction and genetic-interaction ranking relative to evaluated baselines. EMBER also prioritized SCFD1, a mediator of autophagosome-lysosome fusion, as a candidate dependency during mTOR inhibition. Together, these results establish contextualized gene embeddings as reusable building blocks for modeling genetic and pharmacological perturbations, supporting the prioritization of genetic interactions and context-specific interventions for experimental testing.

papers.title_en: RELAY: Relational In-Context Learning for Cellular Perturbation Prediction
papers.authors: Sun, Y., Feng, J., Wang, Y., Xie, W., Zhang, Y., Zhang, X.
papers.evidence: 用关系式上下文学习预测细胞扰动响应
papers.tldr: 细胞扰动响应受扰动身份、细胞类型、供体与剂量等多变量影响，构成多维条件空间，未测条件预测困难。RELAY将相关条件下已测的对照—扰动响应对作为上下文示例，仅利用共享变量关系而非变量具体取值来推断目标响应。在化学、遗传和细胞因子扰动数据上，它在未见过变量取值时优于现有上下文方法，在未见过组合时优于监督扰动预测方法。该工作表明关系型上下文学习可绕开显式变量表示，提升跨条件泛化。
papers.abstract_en: Cellular responses to perturbations vary across multiple experimental variables, such as perturbation identity, cell type, donor, and dose, defining a multidimensional condition space in which each measured population occupies one coordinate. Existing methods predict unmeasured conditions using explicit representations of these variable values, generalizing unseen values therefore depends on the availability and quality of such representations. We present RELAY, a relational in-context model that predicts unmeasured coordinates from measured responses at related coordinates. For each target, RELAY uses measured control--perturbed pairs from conditions that share one or more experimental variables with the target, such as the same perturbation in another cell type. The model receives only which variables are shared, not their values, and uses these demonstrations to predict the target response. We evaluate RELAY on chemical, genetic, and cytokine perturbation datasets under two settings: unseen combinations, where test values are individually observed during training but not in their target combinations, and unseen variable values, where test values are introduced only through context at inference. RELAY outperforms existing in-context methods on unseen variable values and supervised perturbation-prediction methods on unseen combinations. All resources will be open sourced, including code and data.

papers.title_en: RAPTORGraph: graph-based pathway modeling for causal discovery in single-cell perturbations
papers.authors: Adhisantoso, Y. G., Schröder, S. K., Gress, M., Hernaez, M., Voges, J.
papers.evidence: 单细胞扰动中的因果发现与新扰动预测
papers.tldr: 单细胞扰动实验对机制理解与药物发现至关重要，但现有因果表示学习方法在已知干预目标的Perturb-seq场景中难以处理干预溢出，且直接引入通路会带来确认偏误并忽略新信号。RAPTORGraph采用β变分自编码器与GraphPathway编码器显式建模学习通路中的基因互作，并通过预条件隔离扰动基因影响，形成单节点潜在干预。模型还结合最优传输对齐预处理稳定表示。实验显示其在下游未见扰动与非加性互作分析上优于或媲美现有方法。
papers.abstract_en: Experiments involving the perturbation of individual cells are central to understanding cellular mechanisms and can accelerate drug discovery. Causal representation learning allows us to uncover the latent factors that regulate biological systems and predict the impact of novel perturbations. Unfortunately, existing methods fail to address intervention spillover in a closed-world setting where intervention targets are known a priori, such as in Perturb-seq experiments, due to their reliance on dense encoders. Furthermore, incorporating curated biological pathways into the model imposes a confirmatory bias, forcing it to explain the data through preexisting pathways and reducing the set of hypotheses the model can explore, while discarding novel signals that lie outside the annotated pathways. In this work, we introduce RAPTORGraph, a {beta}-variational autoencoder with a GraphPathway encoder that explicitly models complex gene-to-gene interactions within learned pathways. Moreover, our model's preconditioning isolates the influence of perturbed genes, yielding clean, single-node latent interventions required for identifiable causal discovery and eliminating spillover. Finally, we train the model on data preprocessed with optimal-transport alignment, which guarantees a well-defined mapping between control and perturbed samples and further stabilizes the learned latent representations. We demonstrate that RAPTORGraph improves state-of-the-art performance on downstream analyses of unseen perturbations, such as non-additive interactions, while performing competitively on objective metrics, such as mean squared error and maximum mean discrepancy. The source code is available at https://github.com/sXperfect/RAPTORGraph.

papers.title_en: Predicting Transcriptional Responses to Unseen Compounds through Context Modeling and Multi-View Transfer
papers.authors: Lei, Y., Liang, H., Peng, K., Wen, J.
papers.evidence: 通过多视图迁移预测未见化合物的药物诱导转录响应
papers.tldr: 药物诱导转录响应预测对虚拟筛选很重要，但现有模型几乎不利用化合物信息，在drug-blind基准上去掉药物输入后性能变化极小。UnDetect将细胞与实验背景变异同化合物效应分离，融合化学结构、靶点、作用机制和Cell Painting形态，构建可容忍信息缺失的多视图核并跨细胞系迁移残差响应。在drug-blind基准上它每折均优于忽略化合物的网络，板内得分0.117超过最强已发表模型的0.092，DeepCE基准Pearson达0.602。该工作说明分离背景与化合物效应并整合互补信息能提升未见化合物的转录响应预测。
papers.abstract_en: Predicting drug-induced transcriptional responses could support in silico screening of new compounds, yet existing models barely use the compound: on a drug-blind L1000 benchmark, removing the drug input from seven published models changes accuracy by at most 0.012 Pearson correlation. They capture shared cellular and experimental variation while overlooking the compound-specific signals that distinguish drug effects. We present UnDetect, a framework that separates contextual variation from compound effects to predict responses to transcriptionally unprofiled compounds. UnDetect integrates chemical structure, annotated targets, mechanisms of action and Cell Painting morphology into a normalized multi-view kernel that accommodates incomplete compound information, and transfers residual responses within and across profiled cell lines, so that pharmacological and phenotypic relationships inform predictions beyond chemical similarity. On a drug-blind benchmark, where the paired control reveals the assay plate, UnDetect is the only model to beat a network that ignores the compound, in every fold; on a within-plate score that is zero for any compound-blind prediction, it reaches 0.117 against 0.092 for the strongest published model. On DeepCE's benchmark it reaches 0.602 Pearson correlation against the reported 0.491. Transfer across cell lines improves 28 of 28 LINCS L1000 and, at the two higher doses, 47 and 49 of 50 Tahoe-100M cell-line evaluations. These results show that separating context from compound effects and integrating complementary compound information improves transcriptional prediction and extends the utility of perturbation atlases for virtual screening.

papers.title_en: Disentangled generative modeling of single-cell perturbation responses across dynamic cellular states
papers.authors: Wang, Y., Zhao, Y., Li, S., Yang, D.
papers.evidence: 解耦式深度生成模型建模单细胞扰动响应
papers.tldr: 单细胞扰动研究常被细胞周期、状态、供体差异和应激掩盖处理效应。PertVI用解耦变分推断将基线、状态、批次与处理诱导位移分开，并把异常响应隔离到正交空间。模拟与T细胞筛选中，它能区分毒性表型、解析调控子动力学和双相反弹，并发现表型移动与广泛转录扰动解耦。该工作为动态细胞系统的机制化扰动建模提供结构化框架。
papers.abstract_en: Single-cell perturbation studies are increasingly conducted across complex, multi-condition biolog-ical systems, offering a powerful lens into how interventions reshape cell states and molecular pro-grams. However, standard computational models compress single-cell profiles into unified repre-sentations where treatment effects are obscured by cell division, lineage progression, donor varia-tion, and cellular stress. Here, we present Disentangled Variational Inference for Perturbation Re-sponse (PertVI), a deep generative model that separates baseline mitotic phase, cellular state, and batch effects from treatment-induced shifts while isolating aberrant off-manifold responses in or-thogonal anomaly space. This structured design tackles two intertwined tasks: (1) quantifying treatment-induced changes in cell-state composition, and (2) inferring state-gated transcriptional changes in response to treatment. Across simulated benchmarks, PertVI accurately disentangles coupled biological axes and recovers weak treatment signatures. In conditional chemical and genet-ic screens of primary human CD8+ and CD4+ T cells, PertVI separates memory-precursor adju-vants from toxic phenocopies, resolves co-clustered regulators into directional kinetic trajectories and biphasic rebounders obscured by standard workflows, and reveals that treatment-induced phe-notypic shifting is decoupled from broad transcriptional perturbation responses and instead gov-erned by state-specific impulses. Altogether, PertVI brings unique mechanistic granularity to sin-gle-cell perturbation response modeling, serving as a proof of principle for biology-informed, struc-ture-guided variance disentanglement in dynamic cellular systems.

papers.title_en: scAnyOmics: Foundation-Model Distillation for Any-to-Any Completion of Multi-omics Virtual Cells
papers.authors: Zhaoqi Song, Ye Du, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo, Qian Niu
papers.evidence: 多组学虚拟细胞的任意到任意跨模态补全
papers.tldr: 单细胞多组学整合与缺失模态预测仍受配对数据有限制约。scAnyOmics将冻结的单细胞基础模型知识蒸馏到多模态学生模型，把scRNA-seq、蛋白标记和scATAC-seq映射到共享表征。在690,880个细胞及留出供体数据上，它实现跨模态预测与重建并优于基线。该框架统一了不完整多组学整合，支持虚拟细胞建模与知识迁移。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in single-cell technologies have enabled the profiling of multiple molecular modalities, including transcriptomics, proteomics, and chromatin accessibility, providing a more comprehensive understanding of cellular states. However, integrating heterogeneous modalities and predicting missing molecular information remain challenging, particularly when paired measurements are limited. Here, we introduce scAnyOmics, a generative framework that distills knowledge from a frozen single-cell foundation model into a multimodal student model. scAnyOmics integrates scRNA-seq, protein-marker measurements, and scATAC-seq into a shared representation, enabling cross-modal prediction and reconstruction of missing modalities. We assembled 690,880 cells from six publicly available studies, covering both paired and partially paired multi-omics measurements, to systematically evaluate its predictive performance. We further evaluated scAnyOmics on held-out donor data, where it outperformed baseline methods across multiple evaluation metrics. Beyond cross-modal reconstruction, we explored its applications in cell-type annotation, perturbation-response prediction, and biological age estimation. Overall, scAnyOmics provides a unified framework for integrating incomplete single-cell multi-omics data and transferring pretrained biological knowledge, supporting the development of virtual cell models across diverse cellular contexts and experimental platforms.

papers.title_en: HistoTx: Early fusion of H&E images and spatial transcriptomics at varying spatial transcriptomics resolution with self-supervised learning
papers.authors: Alice Driessen, Emil Malmsten, Steffen Wolf, Bernd Illing, Isinsu Katircioglu, Adriano Martinelli, Rolf Stahel, Solange Peters, Enriqueta Felip, Sanjay Popat, Krisztian Homicsko, Raphael Gottardo, Marianna Rapsomaniki, Fei Tang
papers.evidence: 将H&E图像与空间转录组进行多模态早期融合
papers.tldr: 空间转录组与全切片图像联合分析可同时刻画组织形态和分子活动，但现有方法多把转录组当作训练信号，推理仍依赖图像。HistoTx构建任意空间分辨率的转录token，与图像patch token早期融合，经共享Transformer深度交互，并从病理基础模型继续自监督预训练。仅图像推理时多数任务与基线相当，且基因表达预测等任务更优；双模态输入时优于任一单模态。该工作让转录组成为真正输入模态，提升多模态病理建模能力。
papers.abstract_en: Spatial transcriptomics maps gene expression across tissue sections and, when integrated with whole slide images, jointly captures both morphological architecture and molecular activity to provide a rich, multimodal view of tissue biology. ML approaches combining spatial transcriptomics and WSIs typically learn a mapping from morphological features to molecular profiles via contrastive alignment or supervised fine-tuning of pathology foundation models. In both cases, transcriptomics serves as a training signal rather than a true input modality, leaving inference fundamentally image-driven. We propose an early-fusion vision transformer architecture in which transcript tokens are constructed at arbitrary spatial resolution, merged with image patch tokens, and jointly processed through a shared transformer stack for deep cross-modal interaction. Starting from a pretrained vision-only pathology foundation model, we train HistoTx by continuing self-supervised pretraining on paired image and spatial transcriptomics data and demonstrate that: 1) at inference with image only, performance remains on par with the baseline on most tasks while improving on tasks that inherently benefit from molecular knowledge, such as gene expression prediction; 2) when both modalities are available at inference, jointly providing image and transcript inputs outperforms either modality alone.

papers.title_en: When Covariance Is Not Enough: Kernel-Based Regularization for Single-Cell Counterfactuals
papers.authors: Korbinian Traeuble, Edward de Brouwer, Archit Verma, Doron Haviv, Kipper Fletez-Brant
papers.evidence: 单细胞反事实编辑预测干预后的细胞状态
papers.tldr: 单细胞反事实编辑需忠实于个体而非仅条件；概念瓶颈模型常用线性交叉协方差解耦已知与未知因素，但在非线性交互下会失效。作者先用可控仿真揭示一阶准则不足，再引入归一化Hilbert-Schmidt独立性准则作为非线性核正则。仿真中该方法能恢复真实干预效应，复杂scRNA-seq数据上提升不同组织环境下的反事实表达谱生成能力。
papers.abstract_en: Counterfactual editing of single cells, predicting how an observed cell would look had one factor been different, enables in-silico screening where experiments are infeasible, but is useful only if the edit is faithful to the individual and not merely to the condition. Concept bottleneck generative models make the effects of interventions interpretable by decomposing a cell's representation into known and unknown factors. Previous work uses a linear cross-covariance penalty to disentangle known and unknown dimensions. We demonstrate that this first-order criterion does not fully separate information when non-linear interactions are present. We first demonstrate the inadequacy of linear cross-factor penalization with simulation experiments with controlled edits and known non-linear covariate effects. We then demonstrate that adding a nonlinear kernel criterion, the normalized Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion, is able to recover the true intervention effects on simulation data. Finally, we apply the non-linear concept bottleneck model to a complex single-cell RNA-seq dataset and find that it improves the ability to generate counterfactual expression profiles of cells under different tissue environments.

papers.title_en: ExPert infers causal perturbations from cell states across biological and clinical contexts
papers.authors: Schwartz, L., Schlamowitz, J. L., Kuznets-Speck, B., Johnson, C. W., Das, D., Grody, E. I., Bai, T., Sun, H., Senthilkumar, I., Primavera, G., Jung, J., Kuusik, B., Grant, R. A., Rojas, E., Abdrabou, A. M., Peiffer, B., Sun, Z., Diehl, A. M., Marr, C., Chandel, N. S., Mithal, D. S., Weinberg, S. E., Adli, M., Kalsotra, A., Prashnani, E., Goyal, Y.
papers.evidence: 从观测细胞状态反推因果扰动
papers.tldr: 单细胞CRISPR筛选多用于预测扰动后的细胞状态，本文则反向提问：给定观察到的细胞状态，推断其可能的扰动来源。作者提出ExPert，在12种细胞情境共享的潜空间中为每个扰动学习原型，覆盖8964个扰动、1950万细胞。该方法在留出情境上的召回率超过现有最佳方法一倍以上，算力降低1000倍，并可零样本迁移到药物、蛋白降解与组合扰动。在酒精性肝病和原发性线粒体病中，它分别提示mRNA出核异常与受累复合物，并经实验或再分析验证。
papers.abstract_en: Pooled single-cell CRISPR screens have driven substantial effort toward models predicting the response to a perturbation. We posed the inverse question: which perturbation produced an observed cell state? Here we developed ExPert (Extracting Perturbations), which learns one prototype per perturbation in a latent space shared by 12 cellular contexts, trained on 8,964 perturbations and 19.5 million cells, and ranks 19,895 candidate genes per query, over half absent from training. ExPert more than doubled held-out-context recall over the best existing method with 1,000-fold less compute, and transferred without retraining to drugs, protein degradation and combinations. In alcohol-associated liver disease it implicated mRNA export, unchanged in expression, and we experimentally confirmed nuclear poly(A) retention and isoform switching. In primary mitochondrial disease it recovered the affected complex from blood, localized the signal to monocytes, and flagged a misdiagnosed control. Perturbation atlases can thus be queried in reverse, from state to likely driver.

papers.title_en: Resolving how genetic perturbations act through gene regulatory paths
papers.authors: Ren, L., Duren, Z.
papers.evidence: 从Perturb-seq解析遗传扰动经调控路径的作用机制
papers.tldr: Perturb-seq可测大量遗传扰动的转录响应，但单一基因响应混合多条调控路径，仅靠表达量难以解析扰动机制。REGA-perturb用参考表观基因组构建TF—调控元件—基因路径骨架，并借共享潜在程序汇聚扰动响应，推断各路径使用方式且只需RNA数据。在三套CRISPRi筛选共240万细胞中，其TF—靶标推断显著优于现有方法，可区分直接/间接靶标并预测留出TF靶标。该工作还揭示TF活性变化与表达层抵消的调控重连，为扰动机制解析提供可解释路径框架。
papers.abstract_en: Perturb-seq measures transcriptional responses to thousands of genetic perturbations, but each gene's response mixes the contributions of many regulatory paths, so how a perturbation acts cannot be resolved from expression alone, however large the model. Here we present REGA-perturb, which supplies this missing information rather than adding model complexity: reference epigenomes define a scaffold of possible transcription factor (TF)-regulatory element-gene paths, and perturbation responses, pooled through shared latent programs, determine how each path is used, requiring only RNA measurements. Across three CRISPR interference screens totaling 2.4 million cells, REGA-perturb inferred TF-target relationships that agreed with ChIP-seq binding with a gain over random more than four times that of the best existing method, separated candidate direct from indirect targets, and predicted targets of TFs withheld from training. It also inferred perturbation-induced changes in TF activity not reflected in TF transcript levels, and resolved perturbation-specific regulatory rewiring in which opposing regulatory changes cancel at the expression level.

papers.title_en: Generalizable virtual staining from histopathology to spatial proteomics across biological scales
papers.authors: Liu, Y., Falik, O., Zhong, Z., Yu, L., Luo, R., Jin, C., Chen, H., Mayer, A. T., Trevino, A. E., Chou, P., Dai, Y., Wu, Z.
papers.evidence: 从H&E组织学预测空间蛋白的多模态模型
papers.tldr: 常规H&E组织切片缺乏直接空间蛋白测量，但蕴含分子状态相关形态信息。作者提出QUEST，将蛋白标志物表示为语义查询，从配对H&E与MIF图像中学习可泛化的多重免疫荧光预测。模型在逾万个组织区域训练，跨组织类型和队列重建蛋白表达，并支持细胞表型、邻域分析、组织空间结构与患者分层。该工作把虚拟染色从图像生成拓展为连接常规病理与空间蛋白组学的灵活接口。
papers.abstract_en: Large histology archives capture morphological correlates of molecular tissue states but lack direct spatial protein measurements. In this study, we show that routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histology can provide a queryable, morphology-based representation of spatial protein expression that remains informative from pixels to patients. To achieve this, we developed QUEST, a model framework that represents protein markers as semantic queries for flexible multiplex immunofluorescence (MIF) prediction. Trained on a heterogeneous atlas of paired H&E and MIF images comprising over 10,000 tissue regions, QUEST captured morphological patterns associated with protein markers and reconstructed their expression intensities across diverse tissue types and cohorts. Its utility extended beyond image reconstruction and preserved biologically meaningful information across multiple scales: virtual staining preserved protein marker expression at the cellular and tissue scales, supported cell phenotyping, cellular neighborhood analysis, and characterization of spatial tissue organization, retained clinically relevant signals for patient stratification, and enabled H&E-based queries to retrieve MIF references with similar molecular profiles. These findings position virtual staining not simply as image generation but as a flexible interface between routine histology and spatial proteomics, expanding the analytical value of existing H&E archives.

papers.title_en: Where single-cell foundation models help: a benchmark of annotation, perturbation and regulatory inference against simple baselines
papers.authors: Cupaioli, F. A., Merelli, I.
papers.evidence: 在Perturb-seq数据上基准评测原位扰动预测与监督扰动模型
papers.tldr: 单细胞基础模型被寄望通用完成注释、扰动与调控推断，但其真实增益缺乏同数据严格对照。作者在K562 Perturb-seq、原代细胞、脑类器官与肺癌活检上，统一评测五种FM、CellOracle、STATE及任务匹配简单基线。跨物种标签迁移中FM优势明显，Nicheformer达0.98；零样本扰动方向与GRN推断亦有部分增益，而同物种注释仅与PCA相当。研究发布fmaudit基准，明确FM适用边界与后续验证需求。
papers.abstract_en: Single-cell foundation models (FMs) are proposed as general tools for cell-type annotation, in silico perturbation and gene-regulatory-network (GRN) inference. To identify where they add value, we benchmarked five FMs (scGPT, Geneformer V1 and V2, Nicheformer, scFoundation), CellOracle, supervised perturbation models including STATE, and task-matched simple baselines on the same data, from K562 Perturb-seq screens and primary cells to healthy-donor and isogenic leukodystrophy brain organoids, a public organoid CRISPR screen and lung cancer biopsies. FMs were most useful when labels had to be transferred across species: from human to mouse lung, Nicheformer reached 0.98 accuracy and Geneformer V2 and scFoundation about 0.90, against 0.68 for the best baseline. Zero-shot in silico perturbations captured the direction of real responses in K562, with up to 75% of perturbations shifted in the expected direction (scFoundation, p < 1e-8), and Geneformer V2 networks recovered patient-level tumour differential expression better than co-expression (fold enrichment 2.9 versus 2.0). Within a species, FM embeddings annotated cells as accurately as principal components. In organoids, predicted knockout effects were largely explained by where the target is expressed, and an expression-matched control test isolated the gene-specific part, 12 to 35% of the effects. Isogenic Canavan and Krabbe organoids and 4H patient organoids, with one library per line and time point, did not yet separate methods from differences between clones and donors, which defines the replication needed for future validation. Fine-tuning changed classification accuracy but not knockout rankings. We release the benchmark, baselines, pipeline checks and the isogenic reference task as the fmaudit package, so that new models can be evaluated on the tasks where FMs already help.

papers.title_en: Where single-cell foundation models help: a benchmark of annotation, perturbation and regulatory inference against simple baselines
papers.authors: Cupaioli, F. A., Merelli, I.
papers.evidence: 系统评测单细胞基础模型在计算扰动预测中的表现
papers.tldr: 单细胞基础模型被寄望统一完成注释、扰动和调控推断，但其相对简单基线的增益缺少同数据评测。本文在K562 Perturb-seq、原代细胞、脑类器官和肺癌活检上统一比较五种基础模型、CellOracle、STATE及任务匹配基线。跨物种标签迁移优势最大，小鼠肺注释最高0.98，种内注释仅与主成分相当；零样本扰动方向可部分复现，类器官敲除效应多由靶基因表达位置解释。作者发布fmaudit基准与等基因参考任务，明确适用边界和验证需求。

FMs were most useful when labels had to be transferred across species: from human to mouse lung, Nicheformer reached 0.98 accuracy and Geneformer V2 and scFoundation about 0.90, against 0.68 for the best baseline. Within a species, FM embeddings annotated cells as accurately as principal components. We release the benchmark, baselines, pipeline checks and the isogenic reference task as the fmaudit package, so that new models can be evaluated on the tasks where FMs already help.

papers.title_en: LingoCell interprets gene perturbations through natural language and tissue niches
papers.authors: Yang, Y., Xu, W., Zhang, Z., Cui, Y., Yu, X., Gu, W., Wang, J., Nakai, K.
papers.evidence: 单细胞基础模型开展单基因与组合的原位扰动模拟
papers.tldr: 单细胞基础模型难以用生物语言解释表达量变化、迁移到稀疏空间数据并解释细胞微环境。LingoCell将单细胞与空间转录组表征同语言对齐，同时保持基因表达可编辑，支持注释、整合、描述生成和扰动读出。在肺腺癌中，它揭示弱化肺泡分化与强化恶性程序的协同疾病响应；在结直肠癌中，它发现同一成纤维细胞状态向T细胞、巨噬细胞和肿瘤细胞传递不同程序。该框架为靶点组合与基质干预优先级提供统一工具。
papers.abstract_en: Single-cell foundation models are general tools for resolving cell identities and disease states, but struggle to interpret changes in expression magnitude in biological language, to transfer to sparse spatial measurements, and to explain cellular niches. We introduce LingoCell, a foundation model connecting single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. It aligns cell representations with language while keeping gene expression editable, supporting cell annotation, cross-batch integration, description generation, and disease-language readouts of single-gene and combinatorial in silico perturbations. Extended to tissues, it annotates cells without single-cell references, learns identity-conditioned niche embeddings, and performs spatial in silico perturbation by replacing and editing neighbor expression. In lung adenocarcinoma, LingoCell revealed synergistic disease responses to jointly weakening alveolar differentiation programs and strengthening malignant programs. In colorectal cancer, it revealed different programs conveyed by the same fibroblast state to T cells, macrophages, and tumor cells. LingoCell provides a unified framework for prioritizing target combinations and stromal intervention programs.
